title: Mahate ca: the vyāhṛti offerings to the great one
theme: The vyāhṛti offerings again, each adding ‘and to the great one’, and closing with the fourth vyāhṛti, mahaḥ.

words.context: Sāyaṇa: «महते प्रौढाय पूज्याय वा हिरण्यगर्भाय» — to the great, the worshipful, Hiraṇyagarbha

words.role: first of the closing vyāhṛtis (see flags)

words.meaning: mahaḥ, the great — the fourth vyāhṛti
words.context: Bhāskara: «महरोमिति रेफविकल्पः» — in mahar om the r is an optional form

sandhi.rule: ca + antarikṣāya: two a’s merge into ā (cāntarikṣāya).
A visarga becomes ś before c.

sandhi.type: suvaḥ before m; mahar before a vowel
sandhi.rule: suvaḥ keeps its r before a voiced consonant (suvar mahar); mahar joins om (mahar om).

morphology.note: The fourth vyāhṛti, mahaḥ, here written with r before om; Bhāskara calls the r an optional form («महरोमिति रेफविकल्पः») and quotes the Taittirīya’s teaching that mahaḥ is Brahman: «मह इति । तद्ब्रह्म». The word table gives it as printed, since a visarga form would not rejoin into the text.

The base and the Tirupati e-text print भुर्भुवस्सुवर्महरोम् with a short u; the Ānandāśrama text has भूर्. The word is the vyāhṛti bhūḥ; it is listed as printed, and the difference is flagged for review.

translation.literal: Earth: to Agni and to the earth and to the great one, svāhā. Mid-air: to Vāyu and to the mid-air and to the great one, svāhā. Heaven: to Āditya and to the sky and to the great one, svāhā. Earth, mid-air, heaven: to the moon and to the constellations and to the quarters and to the great one, svāhā. Homage to the gods; svadhā to the fathers. Earth, mid-air, heaven, the great — om.
translation.readable: The offerings of the last anuvāka are repeated, each now also made “to the great one”, and the moon is joined by the constellations. Homage to the gods, svadhā to the ancestors. Earth, mid-air, heaven and the great: so be it.

syntax: The frame of 10.4 with each dative series extended by ca … mahate ca, the moon’s series adding nakṣatrebhyaś ca, and the closing vyāhṛtis extended by mahar.

ambiguities.note: Sāyaṇa: Hiraṇyagarbha, the great and worshipful («महते प्रौढाय पूज्याय वा हिरण्यगर्भाय»); the anonymous commentator takes mahate as an adjective of each deity (‘to the great Agni’), adjusting number and gender («महत इत्यग्न्यादीनां विशेषणं वचनलिङ्गविपरिणामेना[न्यत्राप्य]न्वेतव्यम्»). Bhāskara: the great god who is the whole of which the three are parts.

metre.name: prose
metre.note: Prose offering formulas, one printed line of 90 syllables; no metre is claimed.

beginner: This is the third and fullest form of the offering formulas built on bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ and suvaḥ, the old words for earth, the space between, and heaven. Each offering is now made not only to a god and a region but also “to the great one”, and the moon is joined by the constellations. At the end a fourth word is added to the three: mahaḥ, “the great”. The commentators disagree about who the great one is. Sāyaṇa names Hiraṇyagarbha, the first-born creator; the anonymous commentator reads “great” as a description of each god; Bhāskara reads mahaḥ as Brahman, the whole of which the other three are limbs, quoting the Taittirīya Upaniṣad. The anonymous commentator says the offering is made by one who wishes for greatness; the record reports that and claims nothing about its effect.
analogy: Like adding, after each named guest, ‘and the host of the house’, until at the end the host is named alone.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: It repeats the vyāhṛti offerings, adding to each ‘and to the great one’, adds the constellations to the moon and the quarters, greets the gods and fathers, and closes with four vyāhṛtis — bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, suvaḥ, mahaḥ — and om.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The anonymous commentator: offering formulas for one who wishes for greatness — «महत्त्वकामस्य तत्फलका होममन्त्रा उच्यन्ते»; the three deities should grant greatness, being honoured by all («महर्महत्त्वं सर्वपूज्यत्वं दद्युरिति शेषः»). Sāyaṇa: a further reading of the same formulas for one who wishes to be honoured («पूजाकामस्य पुनरप्यन्यपाठमाह»).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhāskara: here the fourth vyāhṛti, which names the supreme Brahman, is taken up in place of the praṇava («अत्र परस्य ब्रह्मणो वाचिका चतुर्थी व्याहतिः प्रणवपर्यायतयोपादीयत इति विशेषः»), and he quotes the Taittirīya’s account of how Māhācamasya made it known: «तासामु ह स्मैतां चतुर्थीम् । माहाचमस्यः प्रवेदयते । मह इति । तद्ब्रह्म».

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: In the closing भुर्भुवस्सुवर्महरोम् the base and the Tirupati e-text print भुर् with a short u, the Ānandāśrama text भूर्. The word is the vyāhṛti bhūḥ; the difference is listed on the sources page for checking. The Tirupati text also misprints महुते once.

schools.disagreement: The commentaries available are ritual and Vedic; none takes a Vedānta-school position here. No Viśiṣṭādvaita or Dvaita commentary on the Mahānārāyaṇa is in the edition’s sources (Raṅgarāmānuja’s is not available here). The commentators differ on who ‘the great one’ is: Hiraṇyagarbha (Sāyaṇa), an epithet of each god (the anonymous commentator), or Brahman named by mahaḥ (Bhāskara).

parallels.note: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad’s Śīkṣāvallī names mahaḥ as the fourth vyāhṛti, made known by Māhācamasya, and calls it Brahman; Bhāskara quotes the passage here.

contemporary.text: Each line names a part — a god, a region — and then adds “and the great one”, as if no part should be named without the whole it belongs to. Remembering the larger thing a task serves, each time one does the task, is a habit worth keeping. This is a modern reflection on the passage, not part of its traditional meaning.

reflect.beginner: Why might a fourth word be added to the three familiar vyāhṛtis only at the end?
reflect.deeper: Is ‘the great one’ a separate deity, an epithet of each deity, or the whole of which they are parts? Which reading does the grammar favour?
reflect.practice: When you finish a piece of work today, name what larger thing it was for.

references.text: Sāyaṇa gives this passage as his anuvāka 4, a variant of the plain vyāhṛti offerings (this edition’s 10.4).

flags.note: The base and the Tirupati e-text print भुर्भुवस्सुवर्महरोम् with a short u; the Ānandāśrama text reads भूर्. The vyāhṛti is bhūḥ; the printed form is kept and listed for checking.
‘The great one’ is read as Hiraṇyagarbha (Sāyaṇa), an epithet of each deity (the anonymous commentator) or Brahman as mahaḥ (Bhāskara).
